 Singapore
 NETS to pilot tap-to-pay for QR payments, with nationwide rollout planned 
 The payment provider will pilot a new QR payment feature as part of its refreshed app, allowing users to initiate payments by tapping their smartphones instead of scanning a code.
 A demonstration of the NETS app's contactless payment function at the NETS booth at the Singapore Fintech Festival, Nov 18, 2026. (Photo: CNA/Wallace Woon)

 SINGAPORE: Consumers may soon be able to pay by tapping their smartphones at NETS payment points instead of scanning a QR code, with the payment services group set to pilot the new feature in Toa Payoh from December. 
 The two-month pilot could be followed by a nationwide rollout if successful, NETS said on Wednesday (Nov 18).
 The new “tap QR to pay” feature allows users with near-field communication (NFC)-enabled smartphones to initiate payments at NETS NFC-enabled SGQR acceptance points without having to open the NETS app first.
 Users will then be taken through a payment process similar to scanning a QR code.

 The feature, which supports both SGQR codes and QR codes generated on payment systems, will initially be available through the NETS app, with support for other participating bank apps and digital wallets expected over time.
 NETS said it is the first to pilot the tap QR to pay functionality via SGQR, Singapore’s single standardised QR code.
 Speaking to CNA at the sidelines of the Singapore Fintech Festival on Wednesday, NETS group chief executive officer Lawrence Chan said the new feature will save users the "extra two or three clicks" to get to a payment, as well as the time spent waiting for an app to load before scanning to pay. 
  "I can be on my email app, I can be reading my football news or queuing up for my coffee, I don't have to get out of the app and can just do my payment," said Mr Chan. "So it really helps the user experience and doesn't compromise safety."
 A demonstration of the NETS app's contactless payment function at the NETS booth at the Singapore Fintech Festival, Nov 18, 2026. (Photo: CNA/Wallace Woon)
 NETS will be responsible for manually replacing merchants' printed QR codes with NETS NFC-enabled SGQR acceptance points as part of the pilot, he added. 
 The pilot comes as NETS rolls out a refreshed app that allows families in Singapore to manage their dependents’ spending through a family wallet, while tourists can also use the app to pay like a local.
 Travellers whose home-country payment apps are not linked to SGQR, such as those from Australia, Europe, or the United States, can now access the local payments ecosystem using the NETS app.
 This follows an earlier announcement last June of Paynow Generation 2, which outlined enhancements to the instant digital payment service, of which NETS is a partner.
 The app, which is accepted at more than 50,000 NETS-enabled SGQR acceptance points, will give overseas visitors a way to pay while exploring Singapore without relying on cash or card acceptance.
 Tourists from China, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam, which already have established QR cross-border linkages with Singapore, can continue to pay directly through their local bank or wallet apps.
 The refreshed app shifts it from a utility-focused payment application primarily serving motorists to a broader lifestyle platform, said NETS.
 "This evolution supports NETS' strategy to deepen consumer engagement by complementing its payment services with relevant lifestyle experiences within a single app experience," the group said.
 One new feature is the family wallet, which allows users to support and monitor family spending. Under the new NETS app, users can use sub-wallets to support the daily spending needs of dependents such as children, elderly family members and domestic workers.
 The primary user can set spending limits and receive notifications of transactions made through the sub-wallets.
 The NETSPay wallet was previously discontinued from the NETSPay app in December 2020, three years after its launch in 2017 .
 Making payments through the NETS app wallet would limit "potential financial exposure" to a user's primary bank account, while maintaining the convenience of digital payments, NETS said.
 Mr Chan said NETS discontinued its e-wallet six years ago due to various business considerations and regulatory changes.
 Having built up a customer base as an app for motoring purposes, Mr Chan said NETS now sees an opportunity to expand its offerings to cater to users' broader lifestyle needs. 
 On the decision to introduce a family wallet, Mr Chan said: "Many like me come from a sandwiched generation where we have to look after our parents and children. Today, with more and more potential scams in the world, we have a product that we think can provide more protection to our wider family."
 Parents can link their children's apps to their accounts, allowing dependents to make payments independently without exposing their banking information. 
 The feature also allows parents to monitor their children's spending and guide them towards better financial habits. 
 "It's not an open checkbook, but it is a way we can help to build a communication bridge with our younger generation, to show them where they are spending, how, why, and ask them why they choose to do this," said Mr Chan. 
 A mini programme module will also be launched in the NETS App towards the end of November, with sub-applications allowing users to shop and access participating merchants' services without downloading a separate app. 
 Mr Chan said the mini programme module will be similar to that of apps like WeChat in China's e-payment system , helping merchants build up loyalty with their customer base by providing new opportunities to engage their customers online. 
 "From an experience standpoint, it's not something new, it's something that many consumers are already very used to. But it's not that readily available in our apps here in Singapore," said Mr Chan.
 NETS Group CEO Lawrence Chan poses for a photo at the Singapore Fintech Festival, Nov 18, 2026. (Photo: CNA/Wallace Woon) 
 The NETS group operates Singapore's national debit scheme, allowing customers of local banks to make payments at over 150,000 acceptance points. Its network also accepts overseas wallet and foreign card payments, such as through apps like Alipay+ and cards from UnionPay. 
 Asked why NETS decided to relaunch its app with new features in a market where users may be spoilt for choice , Mr Chan said the company has "invested well" in strengthening the resilience of its systems and protecting them against cyber threats. 
 "We are really on the path of making ourselves stronger, and only when we do this, can we put in new things to make a difference to the community to serve," he added. 
 "We have to keep on re-inventing ourselves and making ourselves relevant. So it will not stop here."
